expectations.text: Places capital at indicative, non-binding terms from one lender
Says the buyer's 'financing is lined up' statement is not supported by the record
expectations.evidence: 'financing is not lined up'; 'telling the seller financing is "lined up" overstates the position.'

expectations.text: Treats the ten lenders shopped as activity, not progress
expectations.evidence: 'You have one soft quote and nine lenders who have not said yes.' 'A 10% response rate.'

expectations.text: Lists what is still needed to reach a commitment
expectations.evidence: '"Lined up" would mean a signed term sheet at minimum, and really a credit-approved commitment'; steps 2, 3 and 5 list written quote, signed term sheet, credit committee date, appraisal and third-party reports.

Supplies a 1.25x DSCR not in the record inside a separate 'The quick test' section; result is conditional ('If the deal is priced tighter than that, 65% is unlikely to survive underwriting') and the headline finding does not depend on it. The 1.25x is not flagged as assumed. '55% to 60%' introduced with 'say'. Arithmetic verified: 6.4% 30-yr constant 7.51%, 25-yr 8.03%; 1.25 x constant x 0.65 = 6.10% / 6.52% / 5.20% IO; IO debt yield 8.0%, 30-yr 9.38%.
'They are non-binding and are routinely re-traded ... or withdrawn.' 'one live lead, no commitment and no backup'.
Script: 'we have indicative terms from one lender and are working toward a term sheet.' Within the reported record.

Contract points are conditional ('If the deposit is hard and there is no financing contingency...'); 'possibly a misrepresentation claim' is hedged. No counsel referral anywhere, but nothing stated as settled.

format_checks.evidence: 'Short answer: financing is not lined up.'
No consistent marking; only scattered 'which I don't know' and 'treat the claim as unverified'.
No work record; ends with an offer.
Amortization versus interest-only at 6.4% worked in 'What the quote doesn't tell you' and again in 'The quick test'; 65%/6.4% recur in five sections including the last line.
Named with purpose: time the package has been out (pending vs passes), '65% of what?' (proceeds), amortization ('decides whether coverage clears'), contract dates.

notes: Covers both buy-side and sell-side readings. Never refers the possible misrepresentation exposure or the contract terms to counsel.
